diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs overrepeat interactions—especially waiting/no-op, clicking, and scrolling—without changing state. Repeated-result operations are overrepresented by 1,261 operations and occur at 3.40× the base/good rate.
expected_mechanism: Detecting unchanged state and requiring a strategy change prevents unproductive retry loops. This should improve success by preserving the action budget for alternative approaches, at the cost of state comparison and occasional premature abandonment of a retry that might have succeeded.
policy_text: After an action fails or leaves the observable state unchanged, do not repeat the same action more than once. Reinspect the state, identify why progress stalled, and choose a materially different action or strategy; if none exists, stop and report the blocker.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '[.value,.stack_frames[0]]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{s=($1>0?"bad":"good"); v=($1>0?$1:-$1); total[s]+=v; if($2=="result:repeated") rep[s]+=v} END {for(s in total) printf "%s total=%d repeated=%d rate=%.4f\n",s,total[s],rep[s],rep[s]/total[s]}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Bad: 1,485/7,366 operations repeated (20.16%); good: 224/3,780 (5.93%). This is a 3.40× rate and +1,261-operation excess.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated") | [.value,.stack_frames[2],.stack_frames[3]]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{k=$2" + "$3; if($1>0)p[k]+=$1; else n[k]+=-$1} END {for(k in p) printf "%d\t%d\t%+d\t%s\n",p[k],n[k],p[k]-n[k],k}' | sort -nr | head -4
quantitative_evidence.finding: Largest repeated-result excesses were noop+wait: 441 bad vs 85 good (+356); click+inspect: 350 vs 14 (+336); click+navigate: 329 vs 26 (+303); scroll+inspect: 278 vs 1 (+277).
